You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.

"Hey." A woman, maybe 60s, with ink-stained fingers settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 60s, with ink-stained fingers.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
Quiet mending sounds from the bunks — A person, maybe 60s, with deep-set eyes fixing something.
A person, maybe 40s, with freckles came back with 455 kcal of something edible. The pantry breathes.
Nino and Amelia lingered over the fire together.
You remember the Hatchet at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Flannel Shirt at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.

— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.

Amelia Lan reads the sky: clear tomorrow, cold.
A person, maybe 30s will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.

📋 A person, maybe 60s, with a gap-toothed grin — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A person, maybe 60s, with deep-set eyes folds their arms. "Sure. Your call. For now."
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
"Leonard," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Leonard." You'll remember that.

— Nut trees —
Hickories and oaks, heavy with mast. This is a pantry that grows.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
You see smoke on the horizon. Stonebridge — 9 people, 3 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 2 plants — 2 new to you. They've been here the whole time.

Journal: Riparian ground. Water means life, and lunch.

2 unprocessed hauls onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 4 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.

A person, maybe 60s, with a gap-toothed grin spreads the bag on a flat stone and starts naming: Muscadine Grapes ★.
You watch closely — Muscadine Grapes is yours now too.
The bag is empty. Everything named.

A woman, maybe 60s, with tattooed arms spends the afternoon with the tall sunflower-like stalks with knobby tubers at the base, found in sunny patches — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. Edible, but it argues on the way down. The fire's verdict: food, carefully. Small amounts.
From the lumped bag: Jerusalem Artichoke — named, and out.

🛟 the person in their 60s, with a gap-toothed grin stands up by the fire. "The sick can't wait us out. Somebody has to say it, so: we need a plan, tonight. Here's what we CAN do — pick one, maybe two, but everything costs something."
"Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."
"Or we rally," the person in their 60s, with a gap-toothed grin adds. "Second shift, everybody. We work, we eat, we live — and we pay for it."
(Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)
📓 Journal: the person in their 60s, with a gap-toothed grin proposed relief (sickness), day 3.

Fresh-cut stems on the northwest ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Stonebridge's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)
A runner from Stonebridge, dusty and direct: "Your foragers are stripping our side of the northwest ground. Back off — or we'll talk with teeth." (Trust -3. The commons cuts both ways.)
